#  23448 - Numerical Simulation of Nonlinear Structures Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **23448 - module is no longer offered from WS 2026/27**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Numerical Simulation of Nonlinear Structures**  |  
|  Numerische Simulationen nichtlinearer Strukturen   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 6 - Architecture, Civil Engineering and Urban Planning   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Dr.-Ing. Firl, Matthias 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  |  **Knowledge**
  * Formulation of geometrically and/or materially nonlinear engineering problems
  * Principal structure of FE-codes for numerical simulation
  * Numerical methods for nonlinear solution

**Application**
  * Generation of structural models
  * Discretization of structure or fluid
  * Development and specification of appropriate load models for static and dynamic loading
  * Nonlinear solution

**Abilities**
  * Competent use of commercial FE-codes for numerical simulation of nonlinear problems in engineering
  * Verification of results based on engineering competence

 |  
| Contents:  | 
  * Theory and methods of numerical solutions for nonlinear engineering problems
  * Solution of selected engineering problems with practical relevance by application of numerical simulation with commercial codes

Examples will be from the following fields**Civil Engineering**
  * Bridges
  * Tunnels
  * High rising buildings
  * Soil deformations
  * Groundwater flow and mass transport

**Building Physics**
  * Heat transfer problems
  * Heat bridges

**Thermomechanical Problems**
  * Simulation of fire loading on structures

**General Mechanical Simulations**
  * Material testing

**Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering**
  * Metal forming
  * Crash simulation
  * Transport vehicles
  * Engines
  * Wind turbines

 |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | 11144 (MM1), 23427 (MM3)This course should be taken before or simultaneously with this module. A certificate is not required for the registration.  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Seminar / 4 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | 
  * Zienkiewicz, O.C., Taylor, R.L., The Finite Element Method (4th Edition), Vol. 1: Basic Formulation and linear Problems, Vol. 2: Solid and Fluid Mechanics, Dynamics and Nonlinearity, Mc Graw Hill, 1989/91
  * Bathe, K.-J., Finite Element Procedures in Engineering Analysis, Prentice Hall, Englewood Cliffs, NJ, 1982
  * Script Chair Statics und Dynamics
  * Manuals

 |  
| Module Examination:  | Continuous Assessment (MCA)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | 
  * Numerical solution of a nonlinear problem - preferably in context with a current research project at BTU (60%)
  * Presentation, 20 min. and discussion of results (40%)

 |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Remarks:  | SS4In the event that the module cannot be taught or tested according to the present description (e.g. for reasons of infection protection), the alternatives communicated on relevant platforms (e.g. homepage or Moodle) apply.  |  
| Module Components:  | Participation in one of the offered seminars.  |  
| Components to be offered in the Current Semester:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Follow-up Module/s:  |  Phase-out module since: 14.07.2015 
  * without Follow-up Module/s

 |
